transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Evan (Oakridge CTO), Priya (ML Platform Lead), Liam (SRE), Sofia (PM)
---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i see we got a full room. quick agenda: jon will walk through optimize quant profiles, we'll look at int8 vs fp8 quality/latency charts, then scope a pilot. sound good?
[00:11] Evan: yep sounds good. main goal for us is reduce inference cost without a noticeable hit to our nlu quality, we run a lot of short-chat flows and some longer context tasks.
[00:25] Priya: and we care about p95/p99 latency especially for the chat paths, anything above ~350ms starts to feel laggy to product.
[00:37] Jon: great, i'll start with a quick primer on what the profiles are, then show some actual runs from similar customers. so, int8 is our lower precision profile, it's typically the cheapest and fastest but has varying quality impact depending on headroom and model architecture. fp8 sits between int8 and fp16 - it's less aggressive than int8 and often gives a much better quality-latency sweet spot.
[01:05] Liam: quick clarification, when you say int8 do you mean per-channel quantization with calibration, or a more naive symmetric scheme?
[01:11] Jon: good call - we use per-channel asymmetric calibration for most transformer weights plus activation-aware calibration. the profile includes KV-cache handling tweaks and dequantization on the fly to reduce accumulation error.
[01:26] [01:30] Ravi: jam a quick slide: here's a chart from a 1k-sample eval on Llama-2-70b variant - fp8 kept quality within a 0.7% drop (measured by our rouge/qa metrics) while cutting token latency ~35% compared to fp16; int8 shaved ~55% latency but avg quality hit was 2.9% and some corner cases showed hallucination increases.
[01:58] Priya: 2.9% is... borderline for us. can you show distribution? maybe mean vs tail cases?
[02:10] Jon: sure, slide 3 - this breaks down by prompt length. short prompts (<=64 tokens) tend to see smaller quality shifts with int8 because KV cache dominates, long prompts amplify quantization noise because of accumulation across layers.
[02:32] [02:40] Evan: do you have p99 numbers? our SRE cares a lot about tail latency spikes, not just average.
[02:47] Jon: yes, p99 for fp8 was ~1.8x of avg latency and for int8 p99 was ~2.7x - mainly due to occasional dequantization stalls and fallback paths for rare token shapes. we also have batching policy knobs to constrain tail.
[03:07] Liam: are those runs on A100 or on Ampere-like instances?
[03:12] Jon: these runs were on NVIDIA H100s for the fp8 results; int8 tests included both H100 and A100 - int8 benefits more on H100 with tensorcore support, A100 still shows gains but not as large.
[03:29] Priya: how deterministic is the quantization? we need reproducible evals for our CI.
[03:35] Jon: the Optimize flow exports quant profiles and calibration checkpoints. you can re-run the calibration deterministically given the same dataset and seed. we'll share the exact script.
[03:47] [04:00] Maya: can you demo the console quickly - where teams pick profiles and run comparisons?
[04:06] Jon: yup jumping in - (screen share sounds) here's the Optimize tab, model selection, pick Llama-2-70b, choose baseline fp16, then compare fp8-int8 profiles. i run a 1k-sample job right now to show outputs - note the job config uses the customer's response shape and a 1000-sample eval set.
[04:38] [04:45] Jon: showing latency histogram... you can see binning by prompt length, and a quality delta panel that shows per-sample score diffs. i can filter to samples where int8 delta > 5% to inspect failure cases.
[05:05] Sofia: nice, can we link to our internal eval set? we have a labeled set for slot filling and QA.
[05:10] Jon: yes, you can upload a CSV, or we can pull from S3 if you provide creds; for private deployments we support a VPC endpoint so data never leaves your network.
[05:24] Priya: that brings up security - we are SOC2 compliant and will require audit logs and KMS control. what's Redwood's posture?
[05:31] Maya: Redwood supports SOC2 type II, we have KMS integrations, customer-managed keys in private deployment, and full audit logging in the Console. we'll send compliance pack after the call.
[05:45] Evan: perfect. another question on fallback - if int8 triggers a fallback due to detected degradation, what's the automatic path?
[05:53] Jon: we have policy-based fallbacks. you can configure a SLO threshold (e.g., quality delta > 3%) to auto route to fp16 or fp8 variants. there's also a canary window - we run a small percentage on the new profile and monitor before larger rollout.
[06:12] [06:20] Ravi: quick note, the runtime also does prefix caching + KV cache pruning; that can significantly change your latency math for short chats. for Oakridge's chat flows it might be worth enabling aggressive KV caching to reduce token recomputation.
[06:34] Priya: curious about cost numbers - ballpark difference between fp16, fp8, int8 per million tokens?
[06:41] Jon: ballpark on H100s: fp16 baseline cost X, fp8 ~0.65X, int8 ~0.45X - rough numbers, depends on batching and utilization. we'll provide detailed cost model in the spreadsheet.
[06:56] [07:10] Evan: thanks. could we run a pilot that uses fp8 as default and int8 for non-critical batch tasks?
[07:16] Maya: that's a common pattern - fp8 for low-latency user-facing, int8 for background reranking or embeddings.
[07:22] [07:30] Jon: demoing the API route config now - you can set route-level profiles and have model variants. e.g., route /chat use fp8-optimized, route /batch use int8 and a larger batch window.
[07:48] Liam: if we do private deployment on our VPC, will we still get Optimize suggestions?
[07:54] Jon: yes, in Private we can deploy the Optimize agent inside your VPC that reports metrics to your control plane; however audit logs and KMS stay in your environment. there's a short onboarding step to install the agent.
[08:08] Priya: any known quality cliffs for specific model families? we mainly use Mistral and some Llama variants in prod.
[08:16] Jon: Mistral tends to be more sensitive to int8 because of attention head scaling; fp8 is often the safer bet. Llama-derivatives vary - 13b models handle int8 better than 70b in many tests, but you must check with your eval set.
[08:33] [08:40] Sofia: can you walk through the sample failure cases?
[08:44] Jon: sure - looking at int8 failure cluster: rare tokenization sequences, long-document context with repeating patterns, and a small subset of instruction-following prompts that rely on very precise logits. those show higher hallucination. fp8 reduces those issues dramatically.
[09:12] Evan: what's the recommended experiment plan?
[09:17] Jon: we recommend: 1) run calibration on a representative 1k sample set (Priya's eval), 2) run A/B with fp8 vs fp16 for 2 weeks on 10% traffic, track defined metrics, 3) if acceptable roll to 50%, add int8 for batch tasks. we'll provide the playbook and the scripts.
[09:44] [10:00] Priya: ok timeline wise we want a security deep dive before any private pilot. can we do that next week?
[10:06] Maya: yes we'll schedule security deep-dive w/ our security SMEs - propose 2027-01-06.
[10:14] Evan: one more question - our workload has a lot of multi-turn with memory. how does quantization interact with KV cache accuracy?
[10:22] Jon: KV cache is stored in fp16 internally in our runtime for int8 runs to avoid accumulation error; the cost/latency savings are then mostly from weight quantization and matmul kernels. fp8 preserves more fidelity in KV paths.
[10:36] Liam: do you instrument token-level diffs so we can pinpoint where the delta arises?
[10:40] Jon: yes the Optimize tool can output token-level score diffs and alignments for failing samples. it's very helpful for root cause.
[10:50] [11:05] Maya: recap - Redwood will: share benchmark sheet and exported quant profiles, schedule security deep dive 2027-01-06, provide pilot runbook + cost estimate. Oakridge will: provide 1k eval set, share sample traffic profile, confirm pilot nodes.
[11:25] Evan: sounds good. any blockers from our side? we just need the eval set and cost.
[11:32] Priya: i'll get the eval set to Maya by 2027-01-04.
[11:38] Sofia: i'll coordinate calendar for the security call.
[11:42] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and an invite.
[11:48] [12:00] (meeting ends)
